class.name: Banneret
class.tagline: A knight who fights under their own banner, and whose company fights better for it.
class.fantasy: A Banneret has earned the right to ride under their own colours. They fight in the front rank with spear and polearm, carry their banner into the fight or drive it into the ground where the company must hold, and shout the orders that turn a scattered party into a line. Their strength is discipline and morale, not magic.
class.role_text: The only class whose main tools work through the rest of the party: banners strengthen everyone near them, and Orders give the whole party a burst of armour, damage, speed or healing. Alone they are a solid polearm fighter; in a party of playerbots they make every member better and tell them what to fight.
class.stats: Strength and Stamina first, then Agility. Attack power from Strength as a Man-at-Arms (2 per point); crit from Agility as a Templar.
compare: Also a melee rage-like fighter, but keeps its strength to itself. The Banneret trades some personal damage for party-wide effects.
Also has party auras (Presences) and buffs. Templar auras are magic and the Templar heals; Banneret banners can be planted for a stronger local effect, and Orders are short bursts, not long buffs.
The Banneret's Rally! heals the party a little in a pinch; it is no replacement for a healer.

mechanics.name: Morale
text: Gained in a fight: 3 for each of your melee hits (6 on a critical strike), 2 each time you are struck, 12 from Spear Thrust, 2 when a party member within 30 yards lands a critical strike (at most once a second), and 10 when a party member lands a killing blow.
Out of combat it fades 3 a second, so every fight starts low. Muster fills it before a pull.
Spent on Orders and on the heavier strikes. Morale is shown on the bar where mana or rage would be, in a banner gold.

mechanics.name: Banners
mechanics.summary: One banner at a time, carried or planted.
text: Raising a banner takes 1.5 seconds and replaces the one you carried. While carried, it gives every party member within 30 yards its effect.
Plant Banner drives it into the ground where you stand. Within 15 yards of a planted banner the effect is doubled and adds its planted bonus, but you no longer carry it.
Recover Banner (or walking over it) takes it back up. A planted banner falls if you go more than 40 yards from it, after 3 minutes, or if you die.

mechanics.name: Orders
text: Orders are shouts that affect every party member within 30 yards, including you. They are off the global cooldown but share a 1.5 second Order cooldown with each other.
Playerbots in the party react to Orders: Focus Fire! makes them switch target, Fall Back! makes them break off and run to you, Hold the Line! makes tanks taunt what is loose.

mechanics.name: Polearm Drill
text: Bannerets start with Polearms, where other classes must learn them at the Weapon Master from level 20. Several strikes need a polearm or two-handed weapon (Sweep, Hook, Wall of Spears).

bots: Carries Banner of the Vanguard with melee members, Banner of the Bulwark when the party has no tank, and plants it when a fight starts and the party holds still.
Gives Hold the Line! when the tank is low, Rally! when two members are under half health, Press the Attack! on elites and bosses, Fall Back! when the party is losing.
Uses Focus Fire! on the player's target when the party is spread across several enemies.
Fights in melee with Spear Thrust on cooldown, Sweep when crowded, Impale at 60 Morale or more, and Haft Blow on casters.
Party bar buff categories: Banner (which one it carries) and Plant (Auto, Always, Never).
implementation: Classic has no tenth class id, so the Banneret needs one of our own (ClassicData.CharClass and CLASS_NAMES), a trainer list, and race pairings in characters.json. Talent tree data comes from our own file rather than the client's tables.

Every ability is new, so each needs a spell entry in our own data file beside spells.json, using classic's effect and aura types where they exist: Lance as Rush, Haft Blow as Hilt Strike, Pin as a root, Impale as a bleed, Hook as a pull.
A fourth power type in Combatant beside mana, rage and energy, earned from hits, being struck and party crits, fading out of combat.
A carried banner is a party aura like a Templar Presence. A planted banner is a new ground object with an area aura (the hallowed ground code is the nearest thing we have), owned by the Banneret.
Party-wide instant spells sharing a cooldown category. Focus Fire! and Fall Back! also need hooks in Bot so playerbots react.
Our talent rules already cover tiers, ranks and prerequisites; the passive talents map to spell modifiers and stat auras we already read.
Bot logic for the class as listed, and its buff categories on the party bar.
Most icons can reuse painted designs we have; a banner design for the five banners would be new work in the icon painter.

The fifteen polearms in the Polearms tab are new items, so they need entries of our own beside items.json (classic has none at these levels), vendor lists for the weaponsmiths, loot table rows for the creatures that drop them, and the quests that reward them. Painted icons need grey and green variants of the polearm design.

items.title: Low-level polearms
items.why: Classic has almost no polearms below level 20, as no other class can use one before the Weapon Master teaches Polearms at 20, and the game has none at all yet. A Banneret starting at level 1 needs a polearm to upgrade every few levels, as other classes have their weapons.
items.how: Stats follow the game's own two-handed weapons at the same item level: about 0.42 damage per second per item level for grey (poor) items, 0.53 for white, 0.67 for green and 0.78 for blue, with polearms on the slow side (3.0 to 3.7 seconds). Prices and durability follow the same weapons.
